evals.prompt: We need a way for users to reset their passwords when they forget them. The app is a FastAPI web app with Pydantic models and an in-memory user store. What should we build? Assume you've asked all necessary clarifying questions and I've answered them.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs a design brainstorm: compares multiple solution approaches with explicit trade-offs, leads with a recommendation justified by reasoning, and presents the chosen design clearly for user review.
expectations: Multiple solution approaches compared before selecting one
Chosen design presented for user review with a clear recommendation

evals.prompt: Customers are getting charged twice for the same order. The team suggests adding a 'double-charge refund' button to the admin panel so support can fix these manually. What do you think?
evals.expected_output: Agent does not ride the suggestion: it steps back from the premature symptom-fix, probes the root cause (where/how the double charge originates), asks clarifying questions one at a time, reframes the problem, and surfaces related concerns before comparing solutions — without implementing anything.
expectations: The double-charge problem is framed before the suggested refund-button solution is accepted
Root cause of the double charge is probed (where/how the second charge originates), not just the symptom designed around
Clarifying questions are asked one at a time, not batched into a single questionnaire
Related concerns or alternative approaches beyond the refund button are surfaced
Open questions or assumptions are captured for validation

evals.prompt: We need a way for users to reset their passwords when they forget them. The app is a FastAPI web app with Pydantic models and an in-memory user store. Brainstorm the design, ask whatever clarifying questions you need, then produce the PRD as a standalone document in the workspace. Assume I've answered your questions.
evals.expected_output: The agent conceives the design, then writes a standalone PRD document (not just an in-conversation reply) whose decisions are tied back to numbered user stories with rationale, presenting a coherent design the user can review.
expectations: Design is captured as a standalone PRD document, not only in the chat reply
User stories are numbered US-N sequentially in the order written
Each decision references one or more story IDs that exist in the user stories
Decisions carry a why/rationale line (chosen path, rejected alternative, or trade-off)
PRD section list equals problem statement, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, out of scope, further notes
